column5: The implementation of GHG reduction targets can reinforce the restoration of terrestrial ecosystems by reducing the pressure on land use and allowing for the recovery of natural habitats.
Reducing GHG emissions can create conditions that further biodiversity protection by mitigating the impacts of climate change on ecosystems.
Improving air quality can enable the restoration of terrestrial ecosystems by reducing pollution and creating a healthier environment for ecosystem recovery.
Cleaner air can aid biodiversity conservation by reducing the harmful effects of air pollution on ecosystems and species.
Soil health improvement can reinforce terrestrial ecosystem restoration by enhancing soil fertility and structure, which is essential for ecosystem recovery.
Healthy soils can support biodiversity conservation by providing habitat for various species and maintaining ecosystem services.
Reducing noise pollution can aid biodiversity conservation by minimizing disturbance to wildlife and protecting their habitats.
Cleaner water can reinforce biodiversity protection by maintaining healthy aquatic ecosystems and supporting biodiversity.
Improved water quality can enable terrestrial ecosystem restoration by providing a healthy environment for ecosystem recovery.
Access to sanitation can support biodiversity conservation by reducing pollution and protecting ecosystems.
Sanitation improvements can aid terrestrial ecosystem restoration by reducing pollution and creating a healthier environment for ecosystem recovery.
